newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon anxious over Katyusha attack on Israel.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon anxious over Katyusha attack on Israel.

text.p: Lebanese leaders, anxious to prevent an escalation of violence between Moslem guerrillas and Israel in south Lebanon, have called for investigations into a cross-border Katyusha rocket attack on Israel this week.

Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri was quoted on Friday as saying that neither the pro-Syrian Amal Movement he heads nor the pro-Iranian Hizbollah was behind Wednesday's attack on the Western Galilee which caused no injuries.
Israel has blamed Lebanon for the attack. An aide to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Thursday the Israeli army would do whatever was necessary to restore calm.

It was the second Katyusha attack agianst Israel since an April 1996 ceasefire understanding that ended a 17-day Israeli blitz on Lebanon. The U.S.-brokered understanding banned attacks against civilians in northern Israel and south Lebanon.
"This Katyusha rocket was not fired by the Lebanese Resistance; it was not fired by Amal or Hizbollah," Berri told members of the Lebanese Press Association on Thursday.

"It was fired by factions that must be pinpointed through a thorough investigation and must be held accountable for what they are doing," added Berri, whose remarks were published on Friday by Beirut newspapers.
"This matter can cause unrest that we do not need, especially after the commmitments in the April understanding over this and other issues," Berri said.
Hizbollah and Amal are Shi'ite Moslem movements fighting to oust Israel form a south Lebanon occupation zone.

President Elias Hrawi was quoted by the daily an-Nahar as saying: "Israel must not be given a pretext to undertake new assaults. Firing Katyushas is useless militarily and it does not hurt Israel but can harm Lebanon."
The radical Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine-General Command (PFLP-GC) has denied responsibility for Wednesday's attack.
Israel has filed a complaint over the incident with a five-nation group monitoring the April ceasefire.
A similar, mysterious rocket attack took place on December 13. The ceasefire monitors verified the incident but did not reprimand Lebanon or hold it directly responsible.
